text: [I134](iteration134-discrete-geometric-optimization-task.json) receives the original direct brief, hash-bound full recursive task, full report and finalized response. It independently audits all original new paid assertions before screening families 090 (lattice/Riesz/Coulomb energy), 092 (covering density), and 097 (Euclidean Steinitz signing/reordering). Complete source-operation and current primary comparisons are required before developing two routes for the strongest target. S128 will not be reopened this round. I132 discrete-probability discovery and I133 fixed-metric harmonic growth continue. **Eight substantial findings accepted; two remain.**

Four exact screens across lattice energies, covering density and Steinitz balancing select quantitative Gaussian local order. G134 extracts a short-distance quadratic gap from the stipulated atomic deleted-jet operation. P134 combines the periodic Fourier residual, short-pair deletion, saturation, torus Euler counting and a quantitative hexagon lemma. Charging every inserted/deleted point back to original cells yields a uniform bad-site fraction at most C_alpha epsilon^-2 Delta^(1/3), without initial separation. The statement permits independent local orientations.

The density argument is old. Bezdek–Litvak 2009, Theorem 3.1 and its proof, explicitly use a nonnegative density and integrate it along cylinder axes. Their general theorem gives the directionwise ratio lower bound 1/3 in dimension three and the stronger ball/ellipsoid result 1. Their 2016 follow-up, Theorem 3.1, extends this to multiple covers but gives 1/3 again for a single arbitrary-body cover. Its other main inequalities concern packings, not stronger lower bounds for tetrahedral covers. Both papers were read in full, from their primary PDFs. [2009 primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.4842v1); [2016 paper, reviewed v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05115v2).
